learningObjective: Recognize a scenario where operator fusion increases register pressure and causes spill-driven slowdown.

canonicalClaims.claim: Aggressive vertical fusion can widen the union of live ranges beyond the per-thread register file, inducing spills to local memory and dropping occupancy; the net memory traffic of the spills can exceed the DRAM traffic saved by fusion.
conditions: The fused kernel's per-thread register count reported by ptxas exceeds the target's spill-free budget.
Occupancy is a meaningful contributor to latency hiding for this kernel.
nonImplications: Does not imply fusion should be globally disabled; it implies register-pressure-aware fusion partitioning.
Does not imply lower occupancy is always the culprit; some kernels tolerate low occupancy well.

misconceptions.claim: If fusion is correctness-preserving and slower, the compiler backend must be buggy.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Fusion is a heuristic optimization; correct-but-slower is a heuristic failure, not a correctness bug.

misconceptions.claim: Adding pointwise math into a memory-bound kernel is always 'free' since the SMs are stalled waiting on DRAM.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The added work may increase register pressure and cause spills, which are themselves memory traffic; the kernel can transition from memory-bound to spill-bound.

misconceptions.claim: Two sequential kernels on the same CUDA stream overlap execution and are always faster than a fused version.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Same-stream kernels are strictly ordered; overlap requires separate streams and disjoint resources.

misconceptions.claim: Lowering register-per-thread usage always improves performance because occupancy rises.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Forcing lower registers can itself induce spills; the compiler may need more registers per thread to avoid spills.

implementationFacts: ptxas reports register usage and spills via `--ptxas-options=-v`.
On sm_80 with 256 threads/block, 96 regs/thread yields ~25% occupancy (as in A-OCC-003).
Spills to local memory hit L1 first but can spill to L2/DRAM under pressure.
performanceScenarios: A 6-op fusion of pointwise + reduction where the accumulator + 6 intermediates exceed 64 live regs and induce spills.
